correctness.rationale: The scheme is the coefficient reduction of the fixed power-sum ideal. For p≥7 a Jacobian rank drop would force at most two coordinate values; for multiplicities m and 5−m the identity 5s2−s1²=m(5−m)(a−b)² rules this out at a projective solution, including the all-equal case by s1=0. The smooth connected complete intersection has degree 6 and genus 4 by Bézout and adjunction. At p=2 and p=3 the indicated Frobenius relations give the exact redundancy; Jacobian rank two follows since rank loss forces all coordinates equal and then zero. At p=5 translation by the fifth coordinate makes the equations independent of that coordinate. Eliminating the linear form leaves a smooth conic and the product of three lines in the direction plane, each cutting the conic at two distinct F5-points away from the other factor lines. The quadratic and cubic form a regular sequence, so the homogeneous affine cone ring is Cohen–Macaulay and generically reduced with no embedded vertex prime; the projective fiber is indeed reduced, not just set-theoretically six lines. Distinct-coordinate directions are the permutation directions up to scaling and translation; the line stabilizer is the affine permutation group of order 20. The graded normalization quotient has length (6−1)+(6−3)+(6−5)=9 at the only singular point, giving p_a=4. Counting six F5-lines with the single common point gives 6·5^r+1 in every extension and the stated zeta function.
